text.title: Agent Eval Test-Set Curation Core Rules
text.summary: 6 testable rules every application of agent-eval-test-set-curation enforces. Each rule has a statement, a rationale anchored to industry practice, and a source citation.

rule.statement: Golden set has ≥30 trajectories; ≥30% sourced from real production traces (not synthetic).
rule.rationale: Synthetic-only sets miss the long tail; <30 examples lack statistical power for drift detection.

rule.statement: Each trajectory has ≥3 tags: capability (e.g., 'tool-use', 'retrieval'), persona (e.g., 'novice', 'expert'), difficulty (1-5).
rule.rationale: Untagged sets cannot diagnose which capability regressed; harness needs tags to slice subsets.

rule.statement: Every real-trace-sourced trajectory carries a `provenance` field with trace ID, sampling rule, capture date.
rule.rationale: Without provenance, the set drifts and is impossible to refresh from fresh production data.

rule.statement: Golden set is version-controlled at `evals/golden.jsonl`; changes go through PR with reviewer.
rule.rationale: Drift in the eval set is invisible from scores; PR review is the only forcing function.

rule.statement: Set is partitioned: fast-subset tag for ≤20% of cases (stratified across capabilities); full-suite is the remainder.
rule.rationale: Without partition, harness has to manually sample for PR cadence each time.

rule.statement: When neither 100 production traces nor a domain expert is available, the team MUST NOT assemble the golden set from LLM-generated cases alone: a synthetic-only set violates r1's floor of 30% real-trace cases by construction and every entry would lack the `provenance` field r3 requires. Instead the team enables trace capture with the sampling rule written down, defers curation, and records which source is missing (traces or expert) and the trigger that reopens the work (100 captured traces, or expert time allotted).

rationale.source: Ragas documentation on synthetic test-set generation; eval-engineering practice

rule.rationale: Synthetic cases are generated from the same prompt assumptions the agent was built on, so they miss precisely the inputs that break it in production; a set built only from them passes on day one and never catches a real regression. Writing the sampling rule before traces exist is what makes the eventual set refreshable.
